previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her fifth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no acute complications. Her 48-hour methotrexate level showed excellent clearance. An MRI of the head demonstrated a marked reduction in the size of the right frontal lobe lesion, indicating a positive response to therapy. Chronic right foot pain, likely neuropathic, persisted and was managed with gabapentin and oxycodone. Dexamethasone was continued during admission and a tapering plan was provided at discharge. She developed a new lip lesion, presumed herpes-related, and was maintained on acyclovir prophylaxis. She remained stable throughout the admission, with mild transaminitis and anemia monitored but not requiring intervention. She was discharged home with instructions to complete a final day of leucovorin and bicarbonate, and to follow up in two weeks for the next chemotherapy cycle.

rescue PO/IV q6hrs starting 24hrs after MTX.  Anti-emetics PRN.

prophylaxis given hx of oral herpes.  Consulted Social Work for
